treatment.logline: A hotel operations manager demonstrates how a conference enquiry becomes a coordinated quotation, with the final decision still belonging to the team.
treatment.approach: Play the corporate genre as a credible workplace demonstration, not a futuristic product pitch. Warm, directional daylight, controlled reflections and restrained smooth movement support orderly competence. Give the physical display most of the demonstration frame while retaining a readable three-quarter view of the guide performing the explanation: the screen does the explaining without losing the human source. No suspense treatment or unrestricted-access imagery. Parts of long lines change size or setup at sentence boundaries.

editor_notes: The bin contains eight must takes, 58 seconds including handles, against the script-adjusted 47-second target and 70.5-second cap. Use A for the shared welcome, B and C for the opening sentence-boundary changes, D for the readable enquiry, E and F for the live demonstration, and B again for the final human decision. Every dialogue angle performs its own indicated line.

The enquiry, agent and system labels, and Awaiting Approval must remain legible. If screen readability needs a post composite, preserve the exact scripted labels and sequence; do not invent values, permissions, an approval action or a sent quotation.
The two parts of the final long line and the three parts of the opening long line cut at sentence boundaries with changed size or setup. The first and last parts remain on the performing manager.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only possibilities, not requested effects for this restrained business scene. The settled screen and single takes provide clean sources should editorial choose to use them.

Avoid mirrors, hand contact, rapid typing and fabricated system interactions; the screen changes directly without an invented operator gesture. The production timing annotation is never shown or voiced.

The hotel's computer is staged between the standing managers; the earlier scene's computer belongs to another scene and is not carried into this office. Wardrobe appearance and the workstation placement are consistent editorial choices where the packet does not specify them.
